scope: FIFO container using C allocations and byte copies. The main enqueues four 64-bit C-interoperable integers, verifies count and exact retrieval order, frees every popped allocation with C free, checks empty-pop behavior and destroys the queue. No source edits. The implementation uses GNU LOC and raw byte storage; the example makes no portability claim for arbitrary derived types, pointer-owning values, threading or every compiler.
known_limitations: GNU LOC extension and raw byte copying are used by the implementation.

A pointer header follows each payload without general alignment padding. The example uses an aligned 8-byte payload on the x86-64 backend; arbitrary payload widths and other architectures are not validated.
C allocations must be released with C free, as in the consumer.
